title: Quitting Smoking
hook: Your body starts repairing itself within hours of your last cigarette. Quitting is hard and relapse is common — but the right support roughly doubles your odds of success.
key_points: Health benefits begin within hours and days, and keep compounding for years.
Combining counseling with medication or nicotine replacement greatly improves success.
Relapse is a normal part of quitting, not a reason to give up.
Free quitlines and apps offer coaching; in the U.S., call 1-800-QUIT-NOW.
It's never too late — quitting at any age lowers your health risks.
content_html: One of the most encouraging facts about quitting smoking is how quickly your body responds — improvements begin within hours of your last cigarette and keep building for years afterward. The hard part is the addiction, and that's where having a plan and support makes the difference.
extra_html: According to the CDC, quitting at any age lowers your risk of heart disease, lung disease, and cancer, with benefits starting almost immediately. Most people don't succeed on the first try, and slips are a normal part of the process rather than a sign of failure — what matters is getting back on track. The evidence is clear that you don't have to rely on willpower alone: pairing behavioral support, such as counseling or a quitline, with medications or nicotine replacement therapy roughly doubles the odds of quitting for good. Free resources like the 1-800-QUIT-NOW quitline and text or app programs can coach you through cravings and triggers, and a clinician can help match you to the right medication.

source.name: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

related.title: Understanding Addiction
related.hook: Addiction isn't a lack of willpower or a moral failing — it's a treatable medical condition that changes how the brain works. And like other chronic illnesses, it responds to treatment.

related.title: Keeping Your Heart Healthy
related.hook: Most heart disease isn't bad luck — it's the sum of a few everyday habits. The American Heart Association distills them into eight that move the needle most.

related.title: Why Regular Checkups Matter
related.hook: The whole point of a checkup is to catch trouble while it's still quiet — before symptoms show up and while it's easiest to treat.

related.title: Vaping and Cancer: The Evidence Is Mounting
related.hook: A major review concludes nicotine vapes are likely to cause lung and oral cancers — challenging the idea that vaping is a harmless alternative to smoking.

flashcards.prompt: What roughly doubles a smoker's chance of quitting successfully?
flashcards.back_html: Combining counseling or behavioral support with medication or nicotine replacement therapy works far better than willpower alone.

flashcards.prompt: What should you do if you slip and smoke after quitting?

choices.text: Treat it as a normal setback and keep going
Accept that quitting won't work for you
Wait several years before trying again

flashcards.explanation_html: Relapse is a common part of the quitting process. Most people make several attempts before quitting for good, so a slip is a reason to try again, not stop.
